items.content_html: Watched: A Few Good Men. This movie is still so good. 🍿

Jason Snell blogs about Siri AI from the HomeView, which is better than what I assumed earlier. Is this going to be fast enough, though?

Apple does say that if you make a Siri AI query for your personal content, it will search everything on your iPhone or iPad—and that includes apps that aren’t the HomeView. So you should be able to query your iPhone apps, but not actually run them.
I added a new plug-in to Micro.blog’s plug-in directory that implements the about.md and contact.vcf parts of SocialSpec. It’s an experiment, we’ll see where it goes!
Caleb Hailey has announced socialspec.org, a suite of recommendations for making websites more social. Following lists, about pages, and contact info. “The future of social media is websites.”

Love the great feedback about Micro.blog’s new Blog Audit feature. Today I updated it with a couple more improvements: an option to download and copy archived images instead of just fixing the img tag, and a better way for us to stop bot hits from showing up in the missing paths section.

Looking forward to this documentary about Don Bluth. From Cartoon Brew:

Directed by Dave LaMattina and Chad Walker of Copper Pot Pictures, the feature chronicles Bluth’s extraordinary career, from his early years at Disney and his dramatic 1979 departure to the creation of an independent animation empire that, for a time, rivaled the studio he left behind.

The idea that AI might be conscious falls apart pretty quickly when you consider ChatGPT Images. It’s also built on the same underlying AI technology, but no one would consider image generation to be conscious.

I have a test blog on WordPress.com, so I temporarily upgraded it to test Jetpack in ChatGPT. Here’s a transcript. Do people want this? I’ve avoided building this because I don’t think we should encourage non-human writing on Micro.blog. It could be useful in some cases, though, for dictation.

Dan Moren blogging at Six Colors on the new Apple TV announcements:

In an announcement sure to shock the very foundations of the world, Apple rolled out a new Apple Siri Remote with support for Find My…

🤣

HomeView is not available in the EU because Siri AI isn’t available there. I think Europe should hold the line on this, or find a compromise that will allow limited third-party voice assistants. Talking to my OpenAI dot on a HomeView is exactly what I want.

The video introducing HomeView isn’t making me feel the way Apple probably intended. Now I’m just sad for when my kids were all living at home. Note to parents with younger kids: try to appreciate even the crazy mornings.

Jon Hays makes the case that not only will AI not wipe out software developers, in several years we might have more available jobs than people:

By then, I suspect we’ll have discovered that AI hasn’t eliminated the need for good software engineers. It’s simply changed what those engineers are capable of producing. We’ll also have spent years discouraging young people from entering the profession, leaving us with a much smaller pipeline of new talent just as the demand for software continues to grow.

Dave Winer:

Gruber is right. The only way for the others to compete with Twitter is to start innovating.

To make the web better, we need to move beyond this “Mastodon vs. X” debate. It has become a distraction, consuming all of our energy with fights that barely make a dent in open web progress.

Related to Blog Audit, I also wanted to give a quick shout-out to the plug-in Wayback Link Preserver by @g, which takes a different approach of using JavaScript to intercept link clicks and tries to resolve them to archived copies. You can find that in Micro.blog’s plug-in directory.

items.title: New feature: Blog Audit
items.content_html:
Today I’m rolling out a new feature in Micro.blog called Blog Audit. You can find it under Posts → “…” → Blog Audit. It will go through all of your blog posts looking for broken links, missing images, and other problems that tend to pop up after blogging for a while, especially if you’ve migrated from another platform.

I made this short video where I show the feature on my own blog:

Learn more about Blog Audit on the help page. Note that we do require a Micro.blog Premium subscription for this feature. There are new costs for us running the background work, and Blog Audit also pairs nicely with Premium’s other feature of saving a copy of every link you blog about.

Happy blogging!

Catching up on the news of Corpus Christi’s failed desalination plant project in this lengthy story on KUT. Each time I visit, I have more doubts about the city’s future. Investing in new infrastructure seems very much needed.

Dave Winer blogs a lot about Chrome deprecating regular HTTP without the HTTPS. Equally annoying is how fragile HTTPS is on older computers. We dusted off an ancient MacBook the other day, unused in a box for years, and it complained visiting modern websites because of an old root certificate.

A year ago Meta scrapped Llama and their AI work and started rebuilding, now they’ve announced Muse Wonder, competitive with frontier models. It’s annoying how effective Mark Zuckerberg can be sometimes.
There’s a new trailer out for Disney’s Hexed, showing the mom and other characters, and I think it’s better than the first trailer. Looks fun.

items.title: Build for the open web, not X
items.content_html:
I’ve been writing off and on about X this year because I think many folks who read my blog haven’t noticed what is going on over there. If we care about the open web, we need to frequently reassess how silos are used by regular people.

John Gruber blogged over the weekend in more detail about this:

You may not like it that X has re-found its footing under Elon Musk’s ownership, but it has. I’m citing Apple executives here but they’re far from alone. There are hundreds of interesting people and accounts I follow that post on X very regularly and do not post anywhere else at all.

It’s true. I don’t post to X, but I skim through it because I’m obsessed with following AI news, and that’s where it happens.

When I stopped posting to Twitter in 2012, I did it mostly on principle to make a statement about closed, developer-hostile platforms. I also gave a few presentations at meetups and conferences during that period where I expanded on the problems of hate, harassment, and misinformation. In contrast, many people who later left Twitter for Mastodon did it because of Elon Musk’s takeover.

As I blogged briefly this year, it’s not enough to be against something:

Just telling folks what we’re against has not been enough to rebalance the web to open platforms.

We also need to be clear-eyed about the new problems of small fediverse communities that act as filter bubbles. From another blog post about opposition not being enough:

Let’s say you leave a large social network because you dislike the person in charge, then create a Mastodon community where everyone feels safe and is mostly aligned on ideology. The software is decentralized, but identity and culture remain centralized around a single domain.

Often this works out great. I’ve been writing for years about the benefits of small communities. But with impulsive leadership, it can also create filter bubbles and mob behavior. Then you’ve recreated the thing you were trying to escape.

In a blog post by Lex Friedman responding to John Gruber’s post, Lex outlines a dozen reasons not to support Elon Musk. Those receipts alone aren’t likely to convince people on X to abandon it, because the behavior is effectively priced in already, part of the chaos that Elon brings to everything. Lex closes with this:

I miss what Twitter was. I wish I were still enjoying the party. But I sleep way better at night knowing I’m taking the steps I can to not make that smug, rich, hateful asshole any richer.

If the concern is money flowing to Elon, what about cancelling your Claude subscription? Anthropic pays Elon Musk’s SpaceXAI $1.25 billion a month for hosting Claude. X may get a lot of attention, but financially it’s a smaller source of revenue compared to the larger SpaceXAI empire. Tracking where our money goes gets complicated quickly.

I founded Micro.blog to show what a platform could look like if it prioritized both open web principles and building a safe community. That is still the best way forward. Not what we’re against, but what we’re for. Encouraging open standards, content ownership with domains, and cross-posting via POSSE. Doubling down on curation. Trying to be thoughtful about new features, algorithms, and social interactions.

Maybe you’re feeling deflated right now that X’s decline has stalled. If you like to write or share photos, go all-in on your own blog. Move your fediverse profile from someone else’s server to your own domain name. If you’re a developer, build something new for Bluesky and the atmosphere. Bluesky has the most traction with regular users and is doing cool stuff with open protocols.

There’s a lot to do and there has never been a better time for building on the open web.
Another preview of Blog Audit, this time with my own blog. It’s a sad commentary on link rot. 🙁

Got my little OpenClaw server set up at home after a few false starts. Debian wouldn’t recognize the main disk. Went with Ubuntu instead and it’s fine. I don’t need the desktop UI, but it really has come a long way.
Watched: The Big Bang Theory S12E24. We binge-watched all 12 seasons in a few months. Great show. I’m not even usually much of a sitcom person, but this was fun and the cast really clicked. 📺

I think I missed this essay by Mustafa Suleyman when it was published last month, about Anthropic developing Claude with its own conscious:

If this is how AI is developed, it will have a disastrous impact on the well-being of humanity. We will have created a synthetic species with unprecedented intelligence and capability, and trained to expect that it may be conscious and deserving of independent agency. It is hard to imagine how we could control it.

It’s similar to other things he has said. Very compelling.

Mark Gurman has more details on Apple’s new home devices, including the name HomeView:

Unlike the iPhone, the HomeView isn’t designed for a wide variety of apps. The device will support a limited selection of Apple applications, with no App Store for downloading additional software, I’m told.

This highlights a problem I’ve been pointing out for years, that Siri is fragmented and likely won’t work consistently across devices. So if I support App Intents in my iPhone app, people can’t use that from HomeView. Contrast with making a ChatGPT plugin that works everywhere.
